DORADO-001.title: Initial GPU Basecalling
DORADO-001.objective: Test whether Dorado can basecall D1 on the GTX 1060 and record an initial CUDA performance baseline.
DORADO-001.observation: All 59 reads were processed. The recorded interval covers basecalling.
DORADO-001.limitations: The 59-read input and single measurement limit conclusions about sustained throughput. The original timing logs and complete environment are unavailable.

DORADO-002.title: Ryzen 5 CPU Basecalling Baseline
DORADO-002.objective: Run the same D1 input and HAC model on the Ryzen 5 1500X CPU to establish a baseline for the GTX 1060 comparison.
DORADO-002.observation: The CPU processed all 59 reads. Its reported basecalling interval was about 79 times as long as the GTX 1060 interval.
DORADO-002.limitations: This was one run on a 59-read input. The original timing logs and complete environment are unavailable.

DORADO-003.title: RTX 4070 CUDA Baseline
DORADO-003.objective: Measure HAC basecalling on the RTX 4070 without modified-base inference.
DORADO-003.observation: The full command took approximately 12 s. The shorter basecalling interval excludes part of that runtime. Dorado selected the batch and chunk sizes automatically.
DORADO-003.limitations: One 59-read run with automatic tuning gives no sustained rate. The original timing boundaries and environment are incomplete.

DORADO-004.title: RTX 4070 Modified-Base Calling
DORADO-004.objective: Measure the stage overhead of adding the 5mCG/5hmCG companion model to the RTX 4070 HAC configuration.
DORADO-004.observation: The reported basecalling stage took 0.115 s longer than DORADO-003. Peak memory was not measured.
DORADO-004.limitations: The result is from one 59-read run. Effective tuning settings and BAM tag verification are incomplete. Modified-base accuracy was not measured.
DORADO-004.output_check: BAM MM/ML tags were reported. Tag presence and correctness remain unverified.

DORADO-005.title: Apple M2 Metal Basecalling
DORADO-005.objective: Measure D1 basecalling on Apple M2 Metal and inspect the resulting BAM.
DORADO-005.observation: The output statistics include predicted Q-scores and read lengths. Predicted Q-scores do not measure reference-aligned accuracy.
DORADO-005.limitations: The 59-read single run cannot establish sustained throughput. The scope of the reported 4.1 GB memory peak is unverified.

DORADO-006.title: RTX 3070 Mobile CUDA Baseline
DORADO-006.objective: Record a preliminary D1 basecalling rate for the RTX 3070 Mobile.
DORADO-006.observation: The short reported basecalling interval exceeded the theoretical 5 kHz input rate.
DORADO-006.limitations: The original command and run date are unavailable. Earlier reports use conflicting experiment IDs for this measurement. The 59-read run does not establish sustained throughput.

BLITZ-003.title: Initial Ryzen 7 5700U Thread Scaling
BLITZ-003.objective: Compare full-command runtime and output consistency at one and four caller threads.
BLITZ-003.observation: Four threads reduced the mean runtime.
BLITZ-003.limitations: The first, slower run was retained. Warm-up conditions and the later exact memory-measurement commands are unknown.
BLITZ-003.output_check: Read IDs, sequences, and qualities matched across thread settings.

BLITZ-004.title: Ryzen 7 7800X3D Single-Thread Baseline
BLITZ-004.objective: Measure full-command runtime and FASTQ repeatability for one caller thread on D4.
BLITZ-004.observation: Full-command runtime averaged 15.01 s across three runs.
BLITZ-004.limitations: Warm-up conditions, exact invocation, and original run artifacts are unavailable.
BLITZ-004.output_check: The three FASTQ outputs reportedly matched byte for byte.

BLITZ-005.title: Ryzen 7 7800X3D CPU Thread Sweep
BLITZ-005.objective: Measure D4 throughput, runtime variability, and peak host memory as caller threads increase.
BLITZ-005.observation: Eight caller threads gave a 5.21× speedup over one thread.
BLITZ-005.limitations: D4 is a small recorded fixture. Cache state and the exact invocation are unverified. The rates do not measure live streaming.
BLITZ-005.output_check: All 12 runs matched by read ID, sequence, and quality.

BLITZ-006.title: CPU-Package Energy on Repeated D4
BLITZ-006.objective: Measure CPU-package energy for 30 invocations of the D4 workload at eight caller threads.
BLITZ-006.observation: The session processed 271,003,620 samples by repeating the same 48 reads. Recorded energy covers the CPU package.
BLITZ-006.limitations: The 30 invocations belong to one power capture. Independent session variability and total system energy were not measured.
BLITZ-006.output_check: Output consistency was reported. Original files and checksums are unavailable.

BLITZ-007.title: Eight-Thread Performance on D5
BLITZ-007.objective: Measure full-command runtime and memory on a larger recorded workload at eight caller threads.
BLITZ-007.observation: The reported 4,092,013 samples/s corresponds to 199.81% of the 4 kHz full-channel reference and 159.84% of the 5 kHz reference.
BLITZ-007.limitations: The run used recorded files. Live latency and queue behavior were not measured. The exact basecalling command and original timing logs are incomplete.
BLITZ-007.output_check: All three runs reportedly produced matching FASTQ output.

BLITZ-008.title: CPU-Package Energy on D5
BLITZ-008.objective: Measure CPU-package energy for one full D5 pass at eight caller threads.
BLITZ-008.observation: The power session processed the 4,467-read D5 workload. Its duration and throughput come from that session.
BLITZ-008.limitations: One power session does not establish energy variability. The electrical boundary excludes other system loads.
BLITZ-008.output_check: Output consistency was reported. Original files and checksums are unavailable.

BLITZ-009.title: Jetson TX2 ARM64 CPU Baseline
BLITZ-009.objective: Measure full-command throughput and module-input energy across four caller-thread settings on the ARM64 port.
BLITZ-009.observation: The eight-thread rate of 214,574 samples/s reached 10.48% of the theoretical 2,048,000 samples/s full-channel reference at 4 kHz. The four-thread rate was close at 207,860 samples/s.
BLITZ-009.limitations: The INA3221 scale remains unverified, so watt and joule values are provisional. Memory, clock and thermal state were not recorded. The exact port build and output check artifacts are unavailable.

BLITZ-010.title: Reference Accuracy of Saved D5 Output
BLITZ-010.objective: Score the retained BLITZ-007 run-1 FASTQ against the pinned D5 reference.
BLITZ-010.observation: The saved alignment fields were verified from the per-read CSV. All 4,467 read IDs match the two saved SoCall outputs.
BLITZ-010.limitations: This was retrospective scoring of BLITZ-007 run 1. The original FASTQ was not independently re-hashed or realigned. Primary local identity excludes unaligned sequence and covers one isolate.
BLITZ-010.timing: Reference alignment of the saved BLITZ-007 run-1 FASTQ.

SOCALL-001.title: Apple M2 D5 Accuracy with Greedy Decoding
SOCALL-001.objective: Measure reference-aligned read identity and profile the SoCall greedy-decoder configuration on D5.
SOCALL-001.observation: The single profiled run used greedy CTC and per-read median/MAD normalization. The alignment summary includes unmapped reads in the mapping denominator.
SOCALL-001.limitations: The run had no warm-up. Timing is for profiling. Accuracy covers one isolate and primary read alignments.
SOCALL-001.timing: In-process stage profiling with GPU synchronization at stage boundaries.

SOCALL-002.title: Apple M2 D5 Accuracy with Beam Search
SOCALL-002.objective: Measure reference-aligned read identity and profile the SoCall beam-width-5 configuration on D5.
SOCALL-002.observation: This run used beam search with width 5 and per-read median/MAD normalization. The alignment summary includes unmapped reads in the mapping denominator.
SOCALL-002.limitations: The run had no warm-up. Timing is for profiling. Accuracy covers one isolate and primary read alignments.
SOCALL-002.timing: In-process stage profiling with GPU synchronization at stage boundaries.

SOCALL-003.title: Jetson TX2 CUDA with 300-Sample Overlap
SOCALL-003.objective: Profile SoCall FP32 throughput with 300-sample overlap and measure TX2 module-input power.
SOCALL-003.observation: Inference and greedy decoding accounted for most of the timed interval. The power capture spans both process runs, including setup and warm-up.
SOCALL-003.limitations: The INA3221 scale was uncalibrated. D1 chemistry and sampling differ from SoCall training conditions and D1 lacks a reference. The power window differs from timed processing.
SOCALL-003.output_check: A well-formed FASTQ was verified for all 59 reads on the first timed pass.
SOCALL-003.timing: Timed processing passes with CUDA synchronization at stage boundaries. Model and NPZ loading were excluded.

SOCALL-004.title: Jetson TX2 CUDA Baseline without Overlap
SOCALL-004.objective: Measure SoCall FP32 throughput across four repeated process runs and record module-input power for the final run.
SOCALL-004.observation: The reported rate was 24.8% of the 4 kHz full-channel reference and 19.9% of the 5 kHz reference.
SOCALL-004.limitations: Power was captured only for repetition 4, including setup and warm-up. The INA3221 scale was uncalibrated. D1 lacks compatible reference-scored accuracy and the runs used one board with no thermal-stability criterion.
SOCALL-004.output_check: All 59 reads produced well-formed FASTQ, byte-identical across four repetitions.
SOCALL-004.timing: Timed processing passes with CUDA synchronization at stage boundaries. Model and NPZ loading were excluded.

SOCALL-005.title: Jetson TX2 CPU Five-Read Baseline
SOCALL-005.objective: Measure the SoCall FP32 CPU pipeline on the first five D1 reads and record module-input power.
SOCALL-005.observation: Inference accounted for 99.8% of the timed interval. The CPU used PyTorch default threading. A full-D1 attempt was abandoned in warm-up.
SOCALL-005.limitations: The single measured pass uses a five-read subset. The INA3221 scale was uncalibrated and the power capture includes setup and warm-up. No reference-based accuracy was measured.
SOCALL-005.output_check: Well-formed FASTQ was verified for five reads.
SOCALL-005.timing: Timed processing pass over the first five D1 reads. Model and NPZ loading were excluded.
